I often hear gardening mentioned as a way to save money on food. I have a small vegetable garden, and while I definitely enjoy the satisfaction of eating food I've grown, I have a hard time believing it actually saves me money. Soil, fertilizer, seeds and/or plants, fencing, not to mention the spike in my water bill the last few months. It's not a cheap hobby! I've only gotten three cucumbers so far. My pepper plants are quite prolific but in order to use them all I need to preserve them, which is time consuming and another expense. (Supplies to can a jar of jalapeños is around $1 per jar, a store bought jar of jalapeños is only $2) I love gardening and will continue with it regardless of the savings/cost issue, but I would like to hear suggestions for making it more cost effective.
Gardeners of Voat- do you actually save money by growing fruits and vegetables?
I don't buy seeds or soil or anything but food from the store. I take the seeds out put them in my garden and let it go. It has saved me lots of money.

That's awesome you live somewhere it's so easy and cheap to grow stuff! Where I live the ground is mostly rock so I have to buy and haul all the soil and fertilizer. In the Arkansas sun, I have to water every day or all the plants will die. My water bill has gone up about $15 a month this summer.

My girlfriend and I tried a hydroponic system for fresh herbs. I can tell you that it's more for the experience than the produce, and after a fuck-up on my part a lot of them died. It was cool, and we've still got the system. So we're going to try lettuce or something and see if it grows better.

Maybe an outdoor garden would be better, but we're in an apartment right now. Overall, I'd say it's not worth it economically unless you've got quite a large garden and actually do it outside in a place with enough rain.
A hydroponic system would be fun to try. I have read it's much more efficient space and water wise. I've never had good luck growing herbs. They can be finicky. Good luck with the lettuce.

I grow big pumpkins, or should I say I try to grow giant ones. I do it because I like to carve them and as kid we would just get one. So when I got older I went to buy the big ones and found out why I never got them as a kid $$$$. So I grow them and spend double that amount in water and time. I usually get 10 or 15 and carve all I want at Halloween.

I've got some pumpkins growing for the first time. They were a surprise on the side of the driveway where we chucked our Jack o lanterns after Halloween last year. I'm hoping they will produce some for us to carve this year.

Lettuce is cost effective for me because I can pick it as I need it. When I buy it from the store I always have to throw some out. I have chickens, and their poop helps the veg garden, but after feed they are no deal. I just started raising geese, and they don't need feed until winter, so they're a smart addition. They can weed a garden, too, if the crop is right. They won't bother (I've read) tomato or herbs, so next year I'm going to try a goose-garden.
A goose garden sounds interesting. I didn't know they were one of the animals that would weed a garden.

My parents have a huge garden, and it definitely saves them money, and actually earns them some on the side because they sell some of the food. It helps that we live in an area with fertile soil and with a free compost site nearby (we typically cover the garden with 4-6 inches of leaves). Also, fresh vegetables are way better than store-bought.

Oh yes the taste is way better! Having fertile soil and free compost is a great advantage. I would love to have a garden large enough that I could sell some! Sounds like your parents have it figured out!

We have a pretty good garden growing. It is not that expensive after the fencing was all up. We do a lot of our own composting and just buy a little soil and some seeds (say $15/year) and get several months of veg, berries and herbs. But it is a decent amount of work. So from a time perspective it isn't cheap but growing you own food is awesome, tastes better than the store, you know it is organic and is a fun hobby. Buying a bin and composting is way cheaper than buying soil and buying berry bushes that come back every year is a good investment over the long haul.
Composting is a great suggestion. Thank you.

My family has a fairly large garden going in our back yard. No idea if it has helped save any money but it does give us some items that are more expensive or harder to get. Mostly berries, some huge blueberry bushes lining the side of the house, domestic thornless black and raspberries (and some wild blackberries we took from the hills of Ohio that are sour and tart). We do the classic porch tomatoes and peppers (of which there is a wide variety but due to jalapenos and habanero some milder peppers often come out with a punch) and then lastly we try to rotate out either potatoes, green beans or strawberries.

We have too many berries every year and end up giving loads away after the freezers fill up. I also started a couple pecan trees, but haven't really seen much return on them there's still pretty small trees 5-6 years after planting.
